```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  fig.pos = "H",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5
)

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# Locate the project root and analysis folder.
project_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

while (!all(dir.exists(file.path(project_root, c("2-Data", "5-Analysis"))))) {
  parent <- dirname(project_root)
  if (identical(parent, project_root)) {
    stop("Open Yield.Rmd inside the Xilei-Living-cover-crop project.")
  }
  project_root <- parent
}

analysis_dir <- file.path(project_root, "5-Analysis")

# Locate the Clean folder created by the Wrangling document.
folders <- list.dirs(project_root, recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE)
wrangling_dir <- folders[grepl("wrangling$", basename(folders), ignore.case = TRUE)]

if (length(wrangling_dir) != 1L) {
  stop("Expected one Wrangling folder directly inside the project.")
}

clean_dir <- file.path(wrangling_dir, "Clean")

read_clean <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(clean_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop("Missing clean input: ", path, ". Knit Wrangle_Harvest_2026.Rmd first.")
  }
  utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Marketable broccoli yield data

```{r read-clean-yield, include=FALSE}
output_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "Yield_results")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

plot_data <- read_clean("Plot_yield") |>
  mutate(
    block = factor(block, levels = paste0("B", 1:4)),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("T2", "T3", "T4"))
  )

middle_counts <- read_clean("Yield_middle_strip_counts")
plastic_bed_data <- read_clean("Plastic_mulch_bed_yield")
plastic_reference <- read_clean("Plastic_mulch_reference")

living_strip_area_m2 <- unique(plot_data$harvest_area_m2)
plastic_section_area_m2 <- unique(plastic_bed_data$harvest_area_m2)
plastic_ref_kg_ha <- plastic_reference$yield_kg_ha

stopifnot(
  nrow(plot_data) == 12L, !anyNA(plot_data[c("block", "treatment")]),
  all(table(plot_data$block, plot_data$treatment) == 1L),
  length(living_strip_area_m2) == 1L,
  length(plastic_section_area_m2) == 1L,
  nrow(plastic_reference) == 1L
)
```

```{r marketable-head-counts}
knitr::kable(middle_counts, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Weighed and marketable middle-strip heads by treatment")
```

## Fit the living-mulch yield model

```{r yield-model}
# Fit the model using yield per unit area.
fit <- lm(
yield_kg_ha ~ treatment + block,
  data = plot_data
)

anova_result <- anova(fit)

# Adjusted treatment means and Tukey comparisons.
emm <- emmeans(
  fit,
  ~ treatment,
  weights = "equal"
)

emm_table <- as.data.frame(
  confint(
    emm,
    level = 0.95
  )
)

tukey_table <- as.data.frame(
  summary(
    pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"),
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
)

# Confirmed mowing times relative to broccoli transplanting:
# T2: 1 week before, and 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T3: 1 week before, and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T4: 1 week before transplanting only.
#
# Negative weeks indicate time before transplanting.
# Positive weeks indicate time after transplanting.
treatment_labels <- c(
  T4 = "T4\n-1 week",
  T3 = "T3\n-1 and +6 weeks",
  T2 = "T2\n-1, +3 and +6 weeks"
)
```

## Mowing schedule

All three treatments were mown one week before broccoli transplanting.
Additional mowing followed the treatment-specific schedule:

- **T2:** mown at 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving three mowing events in total.
- **T3:** mown at 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving two mowing events in total.
- **T4:** no additional mowing after transplanting,
  giving one mowing event in total.

The analysis compares these three treatment categories.
Mowing times and the number of mowing events are not entered
as continuous predictors.

## Response and experimental unit

Each 4.0 m by 6.7 m living-mulch plot contained three planting strips.
The harvested middle strip covered `r sprintf("%.2f", living_strip_area_m2)`
square metres including interspaces. Marketable head fresh mass was summed
across harvest dates within each plot and converted to kg/ha. Mean marketable
head mass was calculated by dividing the total marketable fresh mass by the
number of marketable heads in that plot.

The yield model compared T2, T3 and T4 across four randomized blocks.
Each plot contributed one yield observation. The model included additive
treatment and block effects.

The two adjacent plastic-mulched beds provided a descriptive reference.
Their eight harvested bed sections covered
`r sprintf("%.2f", plastic_reference$total_area_m2)` square metres including
interspaces. Weather and equipment problems led to different transplanting
times in the living-mulch and plastic-mulch areas.

```{r plot-data}
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::select(
    plot_data,
    block, treatment, heads, yield_kg, mean_head_g,
    harvest_area_m2, yield_kg_ha
  ),
  col.names = c(
    "Block", "Treatment", "Marketable heads", "Fresh mass (kg)",
    "Mean head mass (g)", "Harvest area (m²)", "Yield (kg/ha)"
  ),
  digits = 2,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Marketable broccoli yield and mean head mass by plot"
)
```

## Analysis of variance

Treatment and block are fitted as fixed factors. The design is balanced,
with treatment, block and residual degrees of freedom of 2, 3 and 6.

```{r anova}
# Format display tables without rounding the analysis objects.
format_p <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    "",
    ifelse(
      x < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
  sprintf("%.4f", x)
    )
  )
}

a <- as.data.frame(anova_result)

anova_display <- data.frame(
  Source = rownames(a),
  df = as.integer(a$Df),
  SS = sprintf("%.2f", a[["Sum Sq"]]),
  MS = sprintf("%.2f", a[["Mean Sq"]]),
  F = ifelse(
    is.na(a[["F value"]]),
    "",
    sprintf("%.2f", a[["F value"]])
  ),
  p = format_p(a[["Pr(>F)"]])
)

knitr::kable(
  anova_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
caption = "ANOVA of marketable broccoli yield (kg/ha)"
)
```

## Adjusted treatment means

Means are adjusted for block and expressed in kg/ha.
The table reports each estimated marginal mean, its model-based SE,
and its individual 95% confidence interval.
The figure shows means with error bars of one SE.

```{r adjusted-means}
emm_display <- data.frame(
  Treatment = emm_table$treatment,
  Mean = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$emmean),
  SE = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$SE),
  df = as.integer(emm_table$df),
  Lower = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$lower.CL),
  Upper = sprintf("%.2f", emm_table$upper.CL)
)

knitr::kable(
  emm_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
caption = "Adjusted yield means, SEs and 95% CIs (kg/ha)"
)
```

## Tukey pairwise comparisons

All three pairwise treatment comparisons are of interest.
Tukey adjustment was therefore used to control the family-wise
Type I error rate across these comparisons. Comparisons are based
on estimated marginal means adjusted for block.

Differences, SEs and confidence limits are expressed in kg/ha.
The confidence intervals and p-values below are Tukey-adjusted.

```{r tukey}
tukey_display <- data.frame(
  Contrast = tukey_table$contrast,
  Difference = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$estimate),
  SE = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$SE),
  df = as.integer(tukey_table$df),
  Lower = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$lower.CL),
  Upper = sprintf("%.2f", tukey_table$upper.CL),
  p = format_p(tukey_table$p.value)
)

knitr::kable(
  tukey_display,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Pairwise yield differences with Tukey-adjusted 95% CIs"
)
```

## Yield figure

Negative weeks indicate mowing before transplanting.
Positive weeks indicate mowing after transplanting.

```{r yield-figure}

p <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
aes(x = treatment, y = yield_kg_ha)
) +
  geom_hline(
yintercept = plastic_ref_kg_ha,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "#346B87",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = block),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_table,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      ymin = emmean - SE,
      ymax = emmean + SE
    ),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = emm_table,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(x = treatment, y = emmean),
    shape = 18,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = treatment_labels) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
subtitle = sprintf("Plastic-mulch reference: %s kg/ha",
                   formatC(plastic_ref_kg_ha, format = "f", digits = 0,
                           big.mark = ",")),
x = "Mowing weeks relative to transplanting",
y = "Marketable broccoli yield (kg/ha)",
shape = "Block",
caption = paste(
  "Points show plot yields. Diamonds and bars show adjusted means and one SE.",
  "The dashed line shows the pooled yield from the two plastic-mulched beds.",
  sep = "\n"
)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8)
  )

print(p)
```

## Model diagnostics

Inspect residual spread and the normal Q-Q plot before interpreting the
tests. A non-significant Shapiro-Wilk test does not prove normality.

```{r diagnostics, fig.height=3.5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(fit, which = 1)
plot(fit, which = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

shapiro.test(residuals(fit))
```

```{r save-results, include=FALSE}
a <- as.data.frame(anova_result)
anova_export <- data.frame(
  Source = rownames(a), a, row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(anova_export, file.path(output_dir, "ANOVA.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(emm_table, file.path(output_dir, "Adjusted_means.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(tukey_table, file.path(output_dir, "Tukey_comparisons.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(fit, file.path(output_dir, "Yield_model.rds"))

ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Yield_ANOVA.png"),
  plot = p, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 600, bg = "white"
)
ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Yield_ANOVA.pdf"),
  plot = p, width = 7, height = 4.5, bg = "white"
)

capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_dir, "Session_info.txt"))
```
